/* ═══════════════════════════════════════ PHYSICAL LANGUAGE MODEL DEMO (#plm) ═══════════════════════════════════════ */ #plm { background: var(--bg); } .plm-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.15fr 1fr; gap: 2.5rem; align-items: center; } .plm-preview { overflow: hidden; border-radius: var(--r-lg); display: block; } .plm-svg { width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; background: var(--bg-subtle); transition: transform .4s ease; } .plm-preview:hover .plm-svg { transform: scale(1.02); } .plm-preview-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: .8rem 1.2rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--border); font-size: .8rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-muted); } .plm-live-dot { display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--green); margin-right: .45rem; animation: blink 2s ease-in-out infinite; } .plm-info p { font-size: .93rem; } .plm-stats { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(4,1fr); gap: .7rem; margin: 1.4rem 0; } .plm-stat { background: var(--bg-subtle); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 10px; padding: .7rem .5rem; text-align: center; } .plm-stat b { display: block; font-family: 'Playfair Display', serif; font-size: 1.25rem; color: var(--text); } .plm-stat span { font-size: .68rem; color: var(--text-dim); } .plm-ctas { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .8rem; margin-top: 1.4rem; } @media (max-width: 960px) { .plm-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } .plm-stats { grid-template-columns: repeat(2,1fr); } }
Live Demo · Companion to the Analog-LLM Paper

The Physical Language Model

A Shakespeare-trained neural network that computes with light — no GPU, no CPU. Photons in, letters out.

Interactive simulation — running the real trained weights

Every stage of the roadmap, built and animated: 108 input LEDs shine through inkjet-printed weight masks onto 128 photodiodes; 64 op-amp neurons subtract (pos − neg) and rectify; a winner-take-all circuit picks each next letter — and analog noise on the rails doubles as sampling temperature. The simulation runs the actual trained weights with 16-level quantization and frozen 2% component error — exactly what the soldered machine would compute.

8,166printed weights
64op-amp neurons
108input LEDs
0processors
